transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Daniel Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Aperture Robotics - Head of ML), Chris Wu (Platform Engineer), Samir Patel (CTO)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Aperture's model selection needs for onboard autonomous ops assistant. Focus areas: open model comparisons, context length (32k vs 8k), multilingual support, tool-calling for instrument control, and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). Customer is leaning toward a pilot on hosted but has strict latency and data residency needs that may push to Dedicated or Private.

Topics:
- Current stack and inference constraints
- Model accuracy vs latency tradeoffs
- Context length and KV-cache behavior
- Multilingual and domain-specific performance
- Tool-calling / function calling support and safety
- Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- Pilot scope and timeline

Action items (captured above): pricing, benchmark sheet, sample workload, infra checklist.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Daniel Park: hey everyone, thanks for making time, i'm daniel from redwood - i'll kick off. did you all get the deck i sent?
[00:00:18] Lena Ortiz: yes thanks daniel, we skimmed it, looks good. main thing for us is we want to replace a mix of rule engines and an older llm for our ops assistant - latency under 250ms p95 is ideal for short queries, and we need 1-2s for longer planning prompts.
[00:00:38] Maya Singh: ok that latency number helps, and are you leaning toward hosted api or something in your vpc?
[00:00:45] Chris Wu: initially hosted makes rollout easier but we have to meet gov-ish data residency for some EU customers and also FIPS-kms for keys in some sites. so we might need Dedicated or Private for certain tenants.
[00:01:10] Samir Patel: plus we need tool-calling to orchestrate vehicle subsystems, so function-calling or structured outputs are a hard requirement.
[00:01:25] Daniel Park: got it. quick qualification: current model infra - are you using any internal vector dbs, and what's your token distribution (short vs long)?
[00:01:40] Lena Ortiz: we have a small pinecone setup for embeddings, most queries are short telemetry-to-action prompts ~50-150 tokens but we have long context sessions for mission planning, up to ~15k tokens effective. hope to go up to 32k context for multimodal notes later.
[00:02:05] Maya Singh: ok that's useful - so we should discuss models with long-context support and also efficient kv cache + prefix caching. redwood's runtime has automatic kv-cache reuse for streaming sessions, that cuts cold-token cost.
[00:02:25] Chris Wu: a quick clarification - does dedicated support our quantized fp16/int8 profiles? we want to reduce GPU footprint for production.
[00:02:37] Maya Singh: yes, Dedicated supports quantized weights and we recommend int8 for many of the open models with little quality drop; we can share our quantization matrix. (note: speaker overlap)
[00:02:52] Speaker 2: uh-huh.
[00:03:05] Lena Ortiz: when you say "open models" which ones are in your catalog? we've trialed Llama2 and Mistral but haven't tried Llama 3 or the newer mpt variants.
[00:03:20] Daniel Park: our catalog includes Llama2 family, Llama3 variants, Mistral, MPT, and community-quantized optimized versions. for long context, newer Llama3-large variants and some Mistral-Long models look promising. quality vs cost tradeoffs differ - e.g., Llama3 gives good instruction following but is heavier; Mistral often is cost-efficient.
[00:03:51] Samir Patel: how about multilingual? we need Spanish and Japanese support for field ops.
[00:03:58] Maya Singh: Llama3 and Mistral show decent multilingual coverage; we recommend running prompt tests. we also support custom fine-tuning or lightweight adapters if you need domain-specific terms.
[00:04:20] Chris Wu: tool-calling - how does function calling integrate? can we call out to internal RPCs? we need a secure gateway to actuators.
[00:04:28] Daniel Park: yes function/tool calling is first-class. you can define safe function schemas and redwood streams structured outputs. for private deploys you can host the control-plane in your VPC so tooling is internal.
[00:04:45] Lena Ortiz: any gotchas around latency when using function-calls? the marshal/unmarshal overhead?
[00:04:52] Maya Singh: small overhead but usually negligible compared to generation time. biggest hit is network round trips for external services; we suggest co-locating the gateway and using cached safety checks.
[00:05:12] Speaker 1: right.
[00:05:25] Samir Patel: security questions: do you have SOC2 and ISO certifications, and do you provide KMS/HSM integration for key management?
[00:05:33] Daniel Park: we are SOC2 compliant and have ISO in progress; Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS or HSM integrations and audit logs with per-token tracing.
[00:05:48] Chris Wu: good. on networking, can Dedicated be placed in a customer vpc or is that only Private?
[00:05:56] Maya Singh: Dedicated offers private networking and IP allow-lists, but Private gives you full control of the control plane in your VPC. there's some nuance on peering vs. on-prem air-gapped setups - we can outline options.
[00:06:15] Lena Ortiz: timeline: we want a 4-week pilot proving latency + cost per token on a 10k monthly workload, then expand if numbers look good. procurement will want pricing + SLA.
[00:06:28] Daniel Park: excellent - pilot sounds doable. we'll send a sample TCO and pilot plan.
[00:06:35] Chris Wu: regarding fallback and reliability - do you support model variant fallbacks if a heavy model is busy? we need graceful degradation.
[00:06:44] Maya Singh: yes we support smart routing and automatic fallback to cheaper/compatible variants, plus canary rollouts. that is part of Redwood Optimize recommendations.
[00:06:59] Samir Patel: any benchmarks you can share for p95 latency on 8k vs 32k contexts?
[00:07:07] Maya Singh: we'll share internal bench marks. quick rule-of-thumb: 8k context generation is ~x tokens/sec depending on GPU; 32k incurs memory and kv cache pressure and may increase p95 by ~30-60% unless you use model quant/optimized kernels. we'll include numbers.
[00:07:30] Lena Ortiz: are there any transcription/ai specific mislabels we should watch for?
[00:07:35] Daniel Park: (laughs) we're seeing that too- fireflies sometimes garbles product names, but we'll attach the deck.
[00:07:48] Speaker 3: okay.
[00:08:10] Chris Wu: what about data retention and logs - can we disable retention for PII and store only embeddings locally?
[00:08:19] Maya Singh: yes, for Dedicated and Private you can disable retention, and Redwood supports options to only persist embeddings to your storage. for hosted we have stricter policies but also an enterprise option for no-retention.
[00:08:40] Lena Ortiz: cost sensitivity - do you have an estimate for int8 on Mistral vs Llama3?
[00:08:47] Maya Singh: rough: Mistral int8 can be 30-50% cheaper in GPU cycles versus Llama3; Llama3 may need more mem and larger instance sizes. we'll include specific TCO for your workload.
[00:09:05] Daniel Park: on the pilot, could you share a sample traffic pattern? burstiness, typical concurrency?
[00:09:12] Lena Ortiz: sure - most bursts are telemetry spikes during mission start 200-300 qps for short bursts, steady-state ~20 qps.
[00:09:26] Maya Singh: good to know. we might suggest auto-scaling policies with burst capacity on Dedicated.
[00:09:40] Chris Wu: are there any open-source model licensing issues we should be aware of for commercial use?
[00:09:48] Daniel Park: yes, some Llama-family models have conditions; we can map licensing per model and recommend ones that fit commercial use.
[00:10:05] Samir Patel: do you support A/B testing across models for quality/regression monitoring?
[00:10:11] Maya Singh: yes, redwood console supports rollouts, A/B tests, evals tied to prompt sets and regression alerts. we can hook into your metrics.
[00:10:28] Lena Ortiz: we need multi-language prompt templates - can console handle per-route model configs?
[00:10:34] Daniel Park: yes, per-route configs and per-model token accounting; also token-level cost breakdown.
[00:10:47] Speaker 2: okay.
[00:11:10] Chris Wu: for private deployments, what's the deployment package look like? docker/helm/k8s?
[00:11:17] Maya Singh: private is delivered as customer-managed control plane with helm charts and k8s manifests; we provide an on-prem package and assist with air-gapped installs. HSM integrations require a bit of ops work which we can support.
[00:11:37] Lena Ortiz: any infra constraints for gpu types? we mostly use a mix of A100s and H100s in our clusters.
[00:11:44] Maya Singh: our runtime optimizes kernels per GPU; H100 offers better throughput for FP16/AMP kernels; we can recommend instance types for your workload.
[00:11:58] Samir Patel: are there SLA guarantees for Dedicated? we need uptime commitments.
[00:12:03] Daniel Park: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include the SLA draft in the follow-up.
[00:12:20] Chris Wu: ok procurement note: we also need DPA and data processing terms.
[00:12:25] Daniel Park: noted, procurement will include those in the package.
[00:12:40] Lena Ortiz: quick question on evals - can we run our test-suite to detect regressions after model updates?
[00:12:47] Maya Singh: yes, Redwood Optimize ties to evals and can trigger alerts on regression against baseline prompt sets.
[00:13:05] Samir Patel: i'd like a technical deep dive focused on Private deployment security with your infra team - can we schedule that?
[00:13:13] Daniel Park: absolutely. chris is the right owner to coordinate dates. we'll aim for the week of Aug 24th per earlier note.
[00:13:28] Speaker 1: mm-hmm.
[00:13:40] (several minutes of background chatter and note-taking)
[00:14:30] Lena Ortiz: if we do dedicated, what does onboarding look like and how long?
[00:14:36] Maya Singh: typical Dedicated onboarding is 2-4 weeks: capacity provisioning, network setup, initial benchmarks. Private can be longer depending on air-gap and HSM work.
[00:14:58] Chris Wu: any monitoring hooks for traces and per-token latency? we want to correlate to our APM.
[00:15:06] Maya Singh: yes we have tracing hooks, per-route dashboards, and can emit traces to your tracing stack via OTLP.
[00:15:22] Daniel Park: to summarize action items - we'll send pricing/TCO, benchmark sheet, and schedule the private deep dive.
[00:15:30] Samir Patel: good.
[00:15:44] (short pause)
[00:16:00] Lena Ortiz: another tangential concern: how do you handle hallucinations particularly in safety-critical control prompts?
[00:16:10] Maya Singh: combine structured function-calling with safety filters, and use lightweight verification steps. also prefer models with strong instruction-following and deterministic decoding where possible. we can show tests.
[00:16:31] Daniel Park: additionally, we recommend ensemble checks for high-risk outputs.
[00:16:38] Chris Wu: for the pilot, we want to test a fallback path where the model returns a confidence score and we escalate to a safe policy. is that supported?
[00:16:48] Maya Singh: yes, you can emit structured metadata including confidences, and Redwood's routing policies can escalate or block based on rules.
[00:17:05] Speaker 3: okay great.
[00:17:25] (noise on the line for 10s)
[00:17:40] Lena Ortiz: any constraints about model updates during pilot? we don't want automatic rollouts.
[00:17:46] Daniel Park: we never roll models without customer opt-in for Dedicated/Private; for Hosted we can pin model versions and control automatic updates.
[00:18:02] Chris Wu: last question - are there any regulatory things around EU data residency? can we pin region?
[00:18:09] Maya Singh: yes, you can pin to region; Private and Dedicated can be provisioned in EU regions to meet residency.
[00:18:25] Samir Patel: cool.
[00:18:40] Daniel Park: ok let's recap next steps - i'll send pricing + TCO, maya will share benchmark & quantization guidance, lena will share prompts, chris will gather infra details, and we'll plan deep dive for week of 8/24.
[00:18:58] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. thanks all.
[00:19:10] (call closes; light chatter)

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and auto-caption artifacts. Links referenced: deck (link: redwood-hosted-dedicated-overview.pdf), benchmark sheet (to be shared), SOC2/security deck (to be attached).
